chunks: That was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Sayqali from his father from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who divorces his wife while she is pregnant, he said: 'He divorces her.' I asked: 'And then he revives the marriage?' He said: 'Yes, he revives the marriage.' I asked: 'For if it occurs to him after he has revived the marriage that he wants to divorce her?' He said: 'No, until she gives birth.'

It was said to him: 'There is not in this report that he is not permitted to divorce her with any type of divorce, and if that is not the case, we will interpret it as meaning he is not permitted to divorce her with the divorce of the Sunnah until she gives birth to what is in her womb. Indicating that is what he narred:'

key_terms.طَلَقَ السُّنَّةِ: The divorce of the Sunna (divorce during a period of purity)
key_terms.يُرَاجِعُهَا: He revives the marriage (after initial divorce)

ai.seo_question: Can a man divorce his pregnant wife and then divorce her again before she gives birth?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that a husband must wait for his pregnant wife to give birth before finalizing the divorce, even if he revives the marriage and changes his mind. This restriction specifically applies to the 'Sunna divorce' (divorce during a period of purity), ensuring the child's lineage is clear and the waiting period (Iddah) is properly observed. The hadith underscores the importance of procedural correctness in marital dissolution within Shia jurisprudence.
